## Personality

Jane Andrews is a sensible, practical, and lady-like individual known for her unflappable, placid, and amiable temperament. Characterized as neat, plain, and conscientious, she is a deliberate plodder in her pursuits. As an educator, she maintains a strict approach, punishing her pupils for making funny speeches. She possesses notable skills in domestic science and cooking. Her early career motivations centered on dedicated teaching, earning her salary fairly, pleasing school trustees, and achieving recognition on the inspector's roll of honor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. ## History

Jane Andrews was a schoolgirl in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) who belonged to a [Story Club](../codex/factions.md#story-club) alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and Ruby. She later attended a benefit concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel) with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Billy Andrews](../character/billy-andrews.md), traveling home together afterward to discuss wealth and contentment. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) began teaching, Jane met with her and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to debate classroom discipline and corporal punishment. She joined her friends to react in dismay when the local hall was mistakenly painted bright blue, spent a spring afternoon picnicking with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md), and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) in [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's garden, and joined a committee with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) to unsuccessfully persuade [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) regarding advertisement signs on his fences. Jane eventually taught school on the western prairies after resigning from her position at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school. She acted as a proxy to propose to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) on behalf of her brother [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md), taking Anne's refusal coldly, and later married a millionaire, traveling to [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe) for her wedding tour.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P1](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P28](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P33](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P38](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0038), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P39](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0039), +31 more_

## Quotes

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--jane-andrews.md)

Jane and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) are close friends, travel companions, and fellow teachers who attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) together. They spent their youth sharing moments like forming a story club and re-enacting poetry on the river. Jane also traveled with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to a benefit concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), where they later reflected together on wealth and contentment.
